LESSON: PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.1: Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of Strand 1 in Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should we listen carefully? 2. Why do we take turns when talking?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. identify words with these sounds: /p/ /b/ from print materials such as newspapers, magazines,

2. listen to audio-visual recordings of dialogue containing the sounds /b/ /p/,

3. visualise saying tongue twisters with the sounds /b/ /p/, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. identify words with these sounds: /p/ /b/ from print materials such as newspapers, magazines,
2. listen to audio-visual recordings of dialogue containing the sounds /b/ /p/,
3. visualise saying tongue twisters with the sounds /b/ /p/, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy is enhanced as the learner role plays and constructs sentences using learnt vocabulary.

• Learning to Learn is advanced as the learner builds on their own learning by taking short notes from the text they

have listened to.

• Digital Literacy is developed as the learner listen to audio-visual recordings of words containing sounds /b/ and /p/

in real use.

Values:
Unity is fostered as the learner collaborates with others to engage in role play and answers questions related to the

theme.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life Skills Education: effective communication and self-awareness are enhanced as the learner differentiates the sounds

/b/ and /p/ to communicate clearly.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the content in pronunciation and effective listening to similar concepts as sounds are learnt in

Kiswahili.
